gaps: The plan does not place `--park` inside a rollback boundary. Parking changes the roadmap and story records; if it happens before the upgrade branch, failure changes the original branch. If it happens on the upgrade branch, those changes fall outside the proposed ticket exemption. See docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:54-60 and factory/scripts/check_pr_ticket.py:53-58.

Restoring only `<git-dir>/forge/` cannot prove the promised exact rollback. The planned `forge next` check can write a Git-local `forge-roadmap-healed` marker and can heal `plans/roadmap.json`; neither effect is accounted for in the rollback design. See factory/scripts/forge_cli/phase.py:74-128 and factory/scripts/forge_cli/phase.py:223-233.

A clean harness worktree does not make the existing copy path a copy of committed bytes: it walks the filesystem, and its ignore list excludes only Python caches and `.DS_Store`. The plan needs a committed-source snapshot or a test that rejects other ignored source files. See factory/scripts/forge_cli/upgrade.py:3581-3586 and factory/scripts/forge_cli/upgrade.py:4708-4715.

The proposed ticket exemption omits existing upgrade outputs such as added `.gitattributes` rules, README onboarding, and removal of the old `.gstack/` ignore rule. An older client needing any of these would fail the promised ticket check. See factory/scripts/forge_cli/upgrade.py:4817-4827, factory/scripts/forge_cli/upgrade.py:4859-4882, and factory/scripts/check_pr_ticket.py:44-58.

Path classification and a `Forge-Upgrade` trailer do not prove that a harness-owned file contains the named harness commit's bytes. A hand edit to `factory/` or `WORKFLOW.md`, paired with a rewritten manifest, satisfies the proposed classification and can satisfy the current integrity check. This leaves the explicit hand-made-change rejection criterion unproved. See factory/scripts/check_pr_ticket.py:53-58 and factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:64-85.

The pre-rename proof covers refusal and instructions, but the plan does not test that running the tagged older upgrader and then the new upgrader actually reaches current Forge. That is the only offered route for these clients. See docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:21-26 and docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:116-117.

REBUILD combines replacing a 5,030-line upgrader, parking, rollback, deletions, and the main test replacement in one task without explaining how implementation, proof, three-lens review, and fixes fit one bounded session. The task seam needs a smaller reviewable shape. See factory/scripts/forge_cli/upgrade.py:4593 and WORKFLOW.md:367-380.
contradictions: The plan's exact archive table excludes old grills and approval files, while accepted Decision 0088 explicitly includes them. The current task-plan reader can still direct a client with a legacy task grill to run `forge upgrade`, creating a dead end after the proposed removal. See docs/decisions/0088-simple-upgrade.md:27-32 and factory/scripts/forge_cli/tasks.py:241-251.

The plan promises client-owned docs survive while reusing the doc-contract copy path, which overwrites differing client doc-contract files. A separate active roadmap story specifically addresses this loss and has no dependency or disposition in this plan. See factory/scripts/forge_cli/upgrade.py:4771-4783 and plans/roadmap.json:906-919.

Deleting the sign-off carry without a replacement can turn an older signed-off client into an unsigned one: the current upgrader transfers the legacy `run.json` sign-off into `harness.yaml`, while current phase and board readers require that pin. See factory/scripts/forge_cli/upgrade.py:4829-4858 and factory/scripts/factory_lib.py:624-639.

Reducing the upgrade skill to finish or park, upgrade, and open a PR drops its shipped project backfill and guided pending-story re-authoring flow. The plan names no replacement authority or route for that neighboring user flow. See plans/roadmap.json:395-414 and install/claude/knacklabs-upgrade-project/SKILL.md:92-132.
resolutions: Parking runs on the upgrade branch inside the rollback, and the upgrade commit carries a Parked: trailer per story whose plan move, plan-meta archive and roadmap change the ticket exemption accepts (Technical approach: Run; Ticket check).
Checks run in a throwaway worktree of the upgrade commit, so forge next's heal and git-local marker cannot touch the target; any tracked change they make is a failure (Technical approach: Checks).
Vendoring copies from a committed snapshot of the harness (git archive HEAD into a temp dir), never the working tree (Technical approach: Source bytes).

The ticket exemption now lists every output the upgrader produces: harness-owned paths, manifest, archive renames, .gitignore/.gitattributes blocks and old-rule removals, README onboarding block, sign-off pin, and parked-story changes (Technical approach: Ticket check).

Byte provenance: without harness access the ticket check cannot prove exact harness bytes; the plan states this limit (Risks) and the check refuses changes outside the upgrader's categories; a disguised in-category hand edit is judged by review, consistent with full access (decision 0087).
Verify plan now runs the pre-rename two-step route end to end: the older upgrader from the legacy commit, then the new one, reaching current (Verify plan).
REBUILD is split into CORE (new module), PARK and DELETE-OLD, each one bounded reviewable task (Task decomposition).

The confirmed spec narrowed the archive table; decision 0088's example list is corrected in DOCS-SKILL with the owner's approval carried in the plan approval; the legacy task-grill 'run forge upgrade' advice is reworded to 'finish or park' because no in-flight work crosses an upgrade (What I need from you; Messages).

Doc-contract files follow the byte-ownership rule: client-edited ones are kept and named in the report, never overwritten; the upgrade-preserves-doc-contracts roadmap item is marked covered (Technical approach; Roadmap).
The sign-off carry (legacy run.json sign-off to the harness.yaml pin) is kept, so signed-off clients stay signed off (Technical approach: Run).
The upgrade skill keeps its existing after-upgrade project backfill and pending-story re-authoring steps after following upgrade's printed steps (What changes for you; Docs).
